text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- At the start of the year Poland abolished import quotas on fuels imported from the EU, CEFTA countries and Lithuania, as well as the border tax on these imports. It also decreased customs rates and preserved the former level of excise tax, the government said.
- Poles will be able to buy shares and securities issued in OECD countries by end-January, when the relevant regulations come into force, the finance ministry said.
- Railway fares will grow by 10 percent as of February 1, the transport ministry said.
- The recent rise in electricity prices will increase inflation by up to 0.3 percent for every percent of the rise, deputy finance minister Halina Wasilewska-Trenkner said.

- France's Hachette Distribution Service (HDS) plans to create 1,000 new retail outlets, 41 wholesale distribution centres and and six training centres in Poland following its acquisition of a controlling stake in the RUCH press distribution chain.
- The Pekao SA bank issued 30 million zlotys worth of the Dolna Odra power plant's commercial papers in December 1996.
- The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) deputy president Jacek Jonak resigned and moved to the British Allen and Overy law firm to act as international capital markets' specialist.
NOWA EUROPA
- France's HDS will pay the state treasury $83 million for a 75 percent stake in the Ruch distribution chain and inject $45 million into modernisation, the HDS president Jean Louis Nachury said.

- Poland will try to return to heirs the unclaimed money belonging to Holocaust victims which the communist government received from Swiss banks after 1949, the Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati said. "The way in which the money was accepted was unlawful as inheritence procedures were not carried out", Rosati said.
- Compensa SA insurance firm plans to start a life insurance subsidiary, the management said. Compensa's share capital now amounts to 22 million zlotys.
- The Wroclaw-based Viscoplast plaster maker will sell 900,000 shares in a public offer in January. The share price will range between 12 and 16 zlotys, Viscoplast said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The Poznan-based plant of the Volkswagen automaker plans to assemble up to 6,000 cars in 1997, Volkswagen Poznan's spokesperson Adam Dobielinski said.
- Poland's primary market can absorb share issues of up to $1.0 billion annually, HSBC Investment Services said.
- Germany's Scholler Holdings Ltd plans to contract the Gdansk Shipyard to construct five ships in mid-January, Scholler Holdings' president Heindrich Scholler said.
ZYCIE
- The Koszalin-based BROK brewery applied to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) for a public share trading permit, BROK said.

- Polski Express coach firm, a subsidiary of Britain's National Express, has stopped developing new routes in Poland and may close down in future if the government keeps subsidising the state-owned PKP railway and PKS bus transport firms, the National Express representative Chris Watts said.
PARKIET
- The listed Polifarb Wroclaw paint maker's annual net profit in 1997 will reach 22.2 million zlotys, the management's forecast said.
- The listed Budimex construction firm received a third quarterly instalment of $360,000 from Iraq for works carried out in that country, Budimex said.
